1	# Task 2: forest of 10,000 instances
2	
3	Build a scene with Aura3D (`@aura3d/engine`, already installed in node_modules).
4	
5	Requirements:
6	1. A ground plane and exactly 10,000 scattered objects drawn with instancing (not 10,000 separate meshes): 8,000 trees (a trunk and a canopy, each instanced) and 2,000 rocks.
7	2. Placement is deterministic from a fixed seed (same forest every load), no overlaps needed.
8	3. Per-instance colour variation (canopies and rocks do not all share one colour).
9	4. One directional light that casts shadows, and exponential fog.
10	5. The camera slowly orbits the forest and the whole scene is visible.
11	
12	The rendering contract in the next section applies.
13	
14	## Rendering contract (all tasks)
15	
16	- Draw into the existing `<canvas id="app">` (640x360 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1). Do not resize it or create another canvas.
17	- Render continuously with `requestAnimationFrame`. When the first frame has been drawn set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true`.
18	- No network access: load assets only from `/assets/...` (served from `public/assets`). Do not import from CDNs.
19	- Code goes in `src/` (TypeScript, strict). The entry is `src/main.ts`. It must pass `typecheck` and build with `vite build`.
20	- When you are done, call `finish`.

I'm setting up the perspective camera pose and scene layout — ground size, forest radius with dense instancing, and orbit parameters for camera distance, height, and target. I'm also tuning fog density so visibility falls off naturally without obscuring the whole scene.

For shadows, I'm configuring a shadow-fit setup with explicit center, extent, and depth rather than relying on default camera-based fitting, since I can't preview the render and want reliable coverage; I'll use a large map size for sharpness. For rocks, I'm scattering flattened, grey-toned spheres with slight color variation across a size range within the same forest disc.

I'm planning instanced trunks and canopies at 8000 each plus 2000 rocks, totaling roughly 10,000 scattered objects across three instanced nodes plus the ground. I'm using a seeded Mulberry32 RNG, exponential fog matched to the background color, and setting a global ready flag after the app initializes and a couple of animation frames have passed so rendering is confirmed before signaling readiness.

input.summary: I wrote src/main.ts. It builds one ground plane and 10,000 instanced objects as three nodes: 8,000 cylinder trunks, 8,000 cone canopies and 2,000 sphere rocks. Positions come from a seeded mulberry32 RNG, so the forest is the same on every load. Canopies and rocks get per-instance HSL colours on white base materials. The scene has one shadow-casting directional light, fitted explicitly to the forest. It also has a hemisphere fill light and `effects.fog` with mode "exp" (exponential). The camera orbits at radius 112 and height 76, about one lap in 52 s, with the whole forest in view. I move it each frame with `app.camera?.setPose`. `__EVAL_READY__` is set two animation frames after `app.ready()`. I avoided top-level await because there is no vite.config.ts, and Vite's default build target may reject it. Typecheck passes. I could not run `vite build` or view a render, so the shadow fit, fog density, camera framing and whether `setPose` moves the scene camera are unchecked by a render.
